claim: The same inputs give the same state hash on every machine, forever.
why: The mind must be reproducible: the same experience must give the same mind on any computer, so that every result can be checked by someone else and every change can be traced. If two machines disagreed here, no later test could be trusted.
how: A fixed stream of 4096 pseudo-random words and a bundle of 8 blocks are reduced to a 64-bit fingerprint (FNV-1a state hash). The two fingerprints are compared with values written in the code when the check was created; they must never change.

claim: XOR is undone by itself, has 0 as neutral, commutes, and a XOR a gives point 0.
result: 10 000 random pairs: (a^b)^b = a in 10 000, a^0 = a in 10 000, a^b = b^a in 10 000, a^a = 0 in 10 000
why: XOR is binding: it ties a role to a filler (subject = dog) and unties it again. These four laws are what makes binding reversible, order-free and anchored to point 0.
how: 10 000 pairs of random 64-bit words; each law is tested on every pair and the pairs where it holds are counted.

claim: Every fast operation gives the same answer as its slow, bit-by-bit reference.
result: 2 000 word pairs x 4 operations and 200 bundles of 3 to 8 blocks: 0 differences
why: Fast code is clever and can hide mistakes; slow code is obvious. Every fast kernel of the Monade has a slow twin (the oracle) that reads one bit at a time, and the two must always agree.
how: 2 000 random word pairs through XOR, AND, popcount and Hamming distance, and 200 bundles of 3 to 8 blocks through the majority: fast and slow answers are compared and every difference is counted.

claim: Random vectors are almost orthogonal: they differ on about half their bits, never much less.
result: 1 000 pairs per size; 512 bits: mean 256.3 (expected 256), closest 221, farthest 306; 4096 bits: mean 2049.8 (expected 2048), closest 1924, farthest 2165
expected: mean = half the bits (within 4 standard errors); closest pair above half - 6 sigma
why: The whole memory relies on this: two unrelated ideas look like strangers (about half their bits differ), so a small distance always means a real resemblance and never a coincidence. The larger the vector, the narrower the spread.
how: 1 000 pairs of random vectors of 512 and of 4096 bits; for each pair the number of differing bits (Hamming distance) is counted. The mean must sit at half the bits and no pair may come closer than half minus 6 standard deviations.

claim: A bundle (majority) of k blocks stays close to each of them: each is found again among 100 random decoys.
result: 512-bit blocks, 200 trials each; 3 voices: found 600/600 (100.0%), distance to members 127.9 vs decoys 255.9; 8 voices: found 1 597/1 600 (99.8%), distance to members 186.1 vs decoys 256.1
expected: 3 voices: 100% found (distance about 128); 8 voices: at least 99% found (distance about 186); decoys about 256
why: This is how the blackboard holds several voices in one block: their majority stays recognisably close to each voice. It is memory by superposition, without any training. 8 voices in 512 bits is the size decided for the blackboard.
how: In each of 200 trials, k random 512-bit blocks are bundled by bit-wise majority. Each member must be closer to the bundle than all of 100 random decoys. The charts show the two distributions of distances: members on the left, decoys on the right; the gap between them is the margin of safety.

claim: When the votes are tied, the result is 0: back to point 0, suspension of judgement.
result: 1 000 blocks voted against their opposite: result 0 in 1 000
why: A tie must not be decided by chance: the Monade suspends judgement and returns to point 0. This keeps the vote deterministic and gives the minority (the residue) a defined place.
how: 1 000 random blocks vote against their exact opposite (every bit tied 1 to 1); the result must be all zeros every time.

claim: There are exactly 7 sizes, from 64 bits to 2 MB, each 8 times the one below; any other size is refused.
result: sizes 8 B > 64 B > 512 B > 4 KB > 32 KB > 256 KB > 2 MB: 7/7 match the definition; 7/7 forbidden sizes refused
why: One recursive rule of size at every scale: a Monade is 8 of the size below. Refusing every other size keeps every operation the same at every level.
how: Each of the 7 sizes is compared with its recursive definition in the oracle and converted to bits and back; 6 wrong sizes and level 7 must be refused.

claim: An arena gives back exactly what was put in it, and refuses a Monade of the wrong size.
result: 1 000 x 512 bits: 1 000 identical, wrong size refused; 100 x 4 096 bits: 100 identical, wrong size refused; 2 x 16 777 216 bits: 2 identical, wrong size refused
why: Arenas are the memory of the mind: Monadi of one size side by side, reached by a reference. Nothing may be altered or mixed up on the way in or out.
how: 1 000 blocks, 100 symbols and 2 thoughts of 2 MB are stored and read back; each must be identical, and a Monade one word too long must be refused.

claim: One octal address reaches any part of a Monade, down to one bit; the path is the Morton order of a cube with one point per bit.
result: 512 bits = 512 distinct points of a 8x8x8 cube; 4 096 bits = 4 096 distinct points of a 16x16x16 cube; 10 000 random addresses: round trips (down/up, offset, point, packed) in 10 000, fast = slow in 10 000; 8 digits from 2 MB reach one bit at (255, 255, 255): yes
expected: every bit a distinct point; all round trips; fast = slow; one bit at depth 8
why: One addressing rule for experts, Monadi and bits: each base-8 digit chooses one of 8 parts, i.e. an octant of a cube. Moving down, up or to another tensor is just adding, removing or changing digits, and the same path is a position in space for the visual map.
how: Every bit of a block (8x8x8) and of a symbol (16x16x16) is turned into a point: all points must be distinct. 10 000 random addresses go through every conversion and back, and are compared with slow references.

claim: Basic vectors are computed, not stored: the same id gives the same vector on every machine, different ids are strangers, and any block can be computed alone.
result: fingerprint 0x1125fbd0ff9f9379 (as fixed); 1 000 pairs of ids: mean distance 256.0 of 512, closest 222; any block of a 2 MB vector computed alone: 8/8 identical; speed about 939 MB/s
expected: fingerprint 0x1125fbd0ff9f9379; mean 256; closest above 190; all blocks identical
why: Every axis, role and word of the mind needs its own random vector. Generating them from the seed means they cost no memory until used, are identical everywhere, and form one space per mind: another seed would be another mind.
how: BLAKE3 keyed by the seed (context "monade space v1") turns an id into a stream of bits. The check compares a fingerprint of 64 generated blocks with the value fixed when version 1 was written, measures the distance between 1 000 pairs of generated vectors, checks that any block of a 2 MB vector computed alone equals the same block of the whole vector, and times the generation.

claim: A sentence is one 512-bit block: "the dog sleeps" bound role by role and bundled; asking a role gives back its word.
result: [it.cane it.dormire tempo.presente] soggetto? it.cane (140, next 245), verbo? it.dormire (124, next 246), tempo? tempo.presente (125, next 240); [it.gatto it.correre tempo.passato] soggetto? it.gatto (129, next 242), verbo? it.correre (122, next 234), tempo? tempo.passato (128, next 245); right answers 6/6; smallest margin 105 bits
expected: 6/6 right; each answer near 128 bits, every other word near 256
why: This is composition: several ideas, each tied to its role, held in one vector and taken apart again by asking. It is the first time the Monade represents something built from generated vectors; nothing is learned, it is pure algebra.
how: Words and roles are generated from their names. The sentence is the majority of (subject XOR dog), (verb XOR sleep) and (time XOR present). Asking a role means XOR of the sentence with the role, then finding the nearest word of a vocabulary of 8. A second sentence, "the cat ran", must give different answers.

claim: Point 0 and the specifications are read in canonical form; the seed of the space is locked.
result: folder foundations: point 0 has 0 entries (empty, decided last); 2 specification entries; seed 0x4d4f4e4144450001 locked
expected: both files readable; seed equal to the genesis seed and locked
why: Point 0 and the specifications are the foundations: only the author writes them, nothing can rewrite the past, and the seed that generates the space can never change (a new seed is a new mind).
how: The two files are read from the foundations folder (a missing file means a new mind) and checked for canonical form; the seed must equal the genesis seed and be locked.
